label: Unstable or ECG emergency
detail: Ongoing ischemic discomfort, dynamic ECG change, hemodynamic instability or serious arrhythmia: emergency escalation.

label: Stable, ECG non-diagnostic
detail: Work through the hypotheses, must-not-miss first, with serial high-sensitivity troponin.

label: Respiratory failure or instability
detail: Resuscitate first; the elimination route assumes a stabilized patient.

label: Stable
detail: Work through heart, lung and clot causes in parallel.

label: Positive pregnancy test with pain
detail: Ectopic pregnancy must be considered; ultrasound first.

label: Not pregnant
detail: Choose imaging by suspected source: gynecologic or not.

label: Neurologic deficit or decreased consciousness
detail: A red flag for a secondary cause; the ACEP rule-out tools below do not apply because they assume a normal neurologic exam.

label: Alert, normal neurologic exam
detail: Screen red flags, then apply the SAH rule if the headache peaked within 1 hour.

label: Probable or definite sepsis, or shock
detail: Treat as an emergency: antimicrobials within 1 hour of recognition.

label: Possible sepsis without shock
detail: Time-limited investigation; if infection is likely, antimicrobials within 3 hours.

label: Any high-risk feature
detail: New chest discomfort, breathlessness, abdominal pain or headache; syncope during exertion or supine; palpitations right before syncope; structural heart disease. Evaluate in hospital or with ECG monitoring.

label: Low-risk features only
detail: Typical reflex prodrome or trigger, or syncope on standing up. Likely reflex or orthostatic; discharge can be considered.

label: Not very low risk
detail: Hospital care; endoscopy within 24 hours.

label: Very low risk (Glasgow-Blatchford 0 to 1)
detail: Outpatient follow-up rather than admission, if no other reason to stay.

label: Breathlessness or chest pain
detail: Treat as suspected PE and use that route.

label: Leg symptoms only
detail: Estimate pre-test probability, then test.

label: Continuous dizziness (acute vestibular syndrome)
detail: Stroke must be excluded with HINTS by a trained examiner, then MRI if central or equivocal.

label: Positional (triggered) episodes
detail: Dix-Hallpike for posterior canal BPPV; no CT and no routine MRI.

label: Within a treatment window
detail: Stroke pathway immediately; brain imaging within 25 minutes; other tests must not delay reperfusion.

label: Outside known windows
detail: Still image urgently; the 2026 guideline widens some windows with perfusion imaging.

label: Cauda equina features or severe or progressive deficit
detail: MRI urgently.

label: No red flags
detail: No imaging for uncomplicated pain under 6 weeks.

label: Signs of infection
detail: Covered by the separate ACR acute pyelonephritis topic.

label: No infection signs
detail: Image by patient group.
